newsitem.title: USA: Israel envoy blames Egypt for stall in Hebron talks.
newsitem.headline: Israel envoy blames Egypt for stall in Hebron talks.

text.p: Israel's Ambassador to the United States on Wednesday accused Egypt of encouraging Palestinian leader Yasser Arafat to stall an accord on the Israeli pullout from Hebron, the Washington Times reported.
Eliahu Ben-Elissar also told the paper in an interview that Egypt was pressing other Arab countries not to normalise relations with Israel.

When asked if Egypt was encouraging Arafat to slow down or block agreement on the withdrawal of Israeli troops, Ben-Elissar said, "Yes. Unfortunately, the Eygptians have not been enthusiastic during this process for their own reasons."
Negotiations on the withdrawal, which Israelis have delayed by ten months, have stalled as Israelis and Arabs accuse each other of wrecking any hope for peace.
Ben-Elissar told the Washington Times that Cairo's actions included "besieging Israeli by stopping other (Arab) countries having relations with us as they have done with Oman and Qatar."
He said Israel's negotiations to normalise relations with these two Gulf states had stalled and when the Israeli government explored the reasons, "we found some Egyptian fingerprints along the way."

He said the Hebron talks "could have been settled (by now) since Israelis and Palestinians agreed on the basic thing: that Israel withdraws from the whole part of the city of Hebron where lives Arabs and Moslems -- 95 percent of the city," the newspaper said.
He said he would have preferred to see Egypt play "a more moderate role."
The newspaper quoted Egypt's ambassador to Washington, Ahmed Maher El Sayed, as saying that Egypt is maintaining all the norms of proper diplomatic behaviour in its relations with Israel.
"Nothing... can hide the fact that Egypt faithfully abides by its obligations, and I wish that others would do the same," he wrote in a letter to the paper to be published this week.
